business_problem: Accenture wanted leaders to make decisions from integrated enterprise data instead of siloed systems and needed an IT foundation that could add advanced technologies quickly and cost-effectively, but its legacy on-premises landscape made it harder to scale analytics, scenario planning and generative AI across the company.
solution_summary: Accenture rebuilt its internal IT estate into what it calls a digital core: a composable architecture that is now 95% in the cloud and designed to make data and AI reusable across the business. The transformation integrated operational data from SAP, Workday and Salesforce so leaders could use the 360-degree Value Navigator to see enterprise performance in one place and drill into issues such as bookings projections by market. On top of that shared data model, Accenture added cognitive capabilities and AI-driven scenario planning, then used the same foundation to deploy Copilot for Microsoft 365 and build an integrated generative AI hub that acts as a Center of Excellence for use-case prioritization, skills and delivery. Additional services such as the Identity Trust Engine and SAP finance analytics extend the core, turning cloud, data and AI into an operating platform rather than isolated pilots.
